maya (Design): quick loop 1: account settings form validation: inline as-you-type vs a top-level summary after submit? also we need to pick required-field treatment (asterisk alone or explicit 'Required' label). lastly, delete workspace UX: modal only, or typed-confirm? attaching current mock: https://drive.redwood.design/ux/mocks/account-form-v4.png :mag_right: tom (PM): my preference: inline as default. show top summary only when user submits and there are multiple errors so they get a single place to scan. team should keep copy concise. :ok_hand: liam (A11y): agree with inline-first. accessibility must include: move focus to the first error on submit, use role=alert/aria-live for summary, and don't rely on color alone for error state. asterisk without visible text isn't enough 1 use visually-hidden "required" text or aria-required on input. jess (Frontend): implementation notes: inline validation on blur/typing is easy. top summary needs stable ids so anchors work. example pattern I use: ```html
3 problems found
``` marc (Eng): typed-confirm for org-level destructive ops seems safest (type WORKSPACE NAME or DELETE). for item-level deletes, prefer a short confirm + undo toast. also add 2s debounce on the backend to avoid double requests. zoe (Design Ops): mobile layout: inline messages can push page, so shorten error copy to one line on mobile and rely on icons. we should test on smallest supported breakpoint. maya (Design): proposal: show inline hints & errors during entry (format/length). on submit, if >1 errors, reveal compact top summary with linked bullets. required fields: visible asterisk + sr-only "required" text. delete flow: modal with typed-confirm for org delete; for regular items show a secondary confirm and undo. liam (A11y): +1. small nit: ensure error text contrast meets 4.5:1, and that the summary includes links that are focusable (use ). I can run a quick check after mocks updated. :white_check_mark: jess (Frontend): edge case: server side validation (e.g., email already taken) should appear in summary and map to the related input via aria-describedby so screen readers hear context. we'll need a standard server-error shape. audit-bot: accessibility scan recommended items: focus management, aria-live for dynamic updates, visible text for required fields, color contrast check. maya (Design): next steps: I'll update the prototype to show inline+summary interaction, shorten mobile copy, and add the sr-only required label. tagging @liam for audit once done. sync tomorrow 10:30am. :spiral_calendar_pad:
